name: Biosonar Laryngeal Implant
description: Modifies the larynx to produce ultrasonic clicks and restructures the auditory processing centers to interpret the returning echoes as spatial information. The user gains functional echolocation — the ability to 'see' the shape and distance of objects in complete darkness through sound. The clicks are above normal human hearing range but audible to dogs, cats, and other echolocation users. The neural processing component is the difficult part — the brain must be trained to interpret echo data as spatial awareness, which typically takes 3–6 months of practice. Skilled users report the sensation as a 'pressure map' overlaid on their normal spatial awareness. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's version includes enhanced cochlear sensitivity that allows echolocation in noisy environments by filtering ambient sound. Echolocation users often develop a distinctive head-tilting behavior as they orient their click emissions.
source_organism: Rousettus aegyptiacus (Egyptian fruit bat), Physeter macrocephalus (sperm whale, deep-frequency variant)
procedure: Laryngeal microsurgery with retroviral neural pathway induction, 1 surgical session + 6 neural integration sessions
expression_time: 2 weeks physical; 3–6 months for functional echolocation
reversibility: Laryngeal modification reversible; neural pathway changes are permanent
side_effects: Involuntary clicking during stress or sleep
Disorientation in acoustically dead environments (soundproofed rooms)
Other echolocation users can hear your clicks — no stealth between bat-users
social_perception: Respected as a serious functional modification. Users are sometimes called 'bats' — the term ranges from affectionate to derogatory depending on context. Valued in security, rescue, and underground exploration professions.
story_hooks: An echolocation user detects a hidden room behind a wall that doesn't appear on any building plans
A community of echolocation users in the deep the Gray Zone communicates through click-patterns that have evolved into a rudimentary language inaudible to outsiders
